earnings_calls.summary: Management framed the quarter as part of the shift from technology development to commercialization, aimed at AI and data-center optical interconnects. The company said five Fortune Global 500 companies are now in advanced prototype (Stage 3) programs, with a broader pipeline of roughly 20 companies. Losses widened as R&D and G&A each rose close to 50% year over year. Management guided that 2026 revenue stays limited to material supply, NRE and prototype work, with volume production targeted for the second half of 2027 and Q4 2026 expected to be busy with wafer deliveries and customer testing.
key_points: Five Fortune Global 500 customers in Stage 3 / advanced prototype programs; pipeline around 20 companies
Revenue model: direct electro-optic polymer material sales plus IP licensing
Volume production targeted for 2H 2027; meaningful production revenue not expected before 2027
Q4 2026 milestones: wafer deliveries, back-end processing, customer testing
Cash plus marketable securities about $95.9M; company says funded through at least December 2027
ATM sales in Q2 2026: 1,794,185 shares for ~$21.3M net; ATM (upsized to $51.4M in April 2026) essentially exhausted
Fred Graffam appointed CFO on July 20, 2026 (after quarter end)

earnings_calls.summary: The company raised its 2028 AI/data-center optical transceiver market estimate to about $47B (from about $17B) and sized the serviceable market for EO polymer modulators at $2-4B. Four Fortune 500/Global 500 customers were at the prototyping stage, with one or two more expected by end of Q3 2026. Management flagged foundry capacity limits and long silicon photonics fab cycles as the main pacing items, and said it was standing up a new production line in Denver. Cash was about $75M at quarter end and roughly $100M by May 11 after using up the August 2024 shelf.
key_points: 2028 TAM estimate raised to ~$47B; SAM for EO polymer modulators $2-4B
Four F500/Global 500 customers in prototyping; 1-2 more expected by end of Q3 2026
Foundry capacity and fab cycle times slowing path to manufacturing
New Denver production line being prepared for ramp
Cash ~$75M at 3/31/26; ~$100M by 5/11/26 after shelf/ATM use
short_quotes: "AI connectivity is becoming just as critical as computing power itself." - Yves LeMaitre, CEO

earnings_calls.summary: Management called 2025 an execution year that moved the company from research validation into structured commercialization. Three customer programs reached Stage 3 during 2025 and a fourth followed in early 2026, with roughly 15 more engagements in earlier stages. Foundry agreements were in place with four foundries, including SilTerra and GlobalFoundries, with wafer runs planned for 1H 2026. Year-end cash was about $69M, helped by a January 2026 public offering, and management said that funds operations beyond December 2027.
key_points: FY2025 revenue ~$237K, mostly licensing/NRE (up from ~$96K in 2024)
FY2025 net loss $20.3M ($0.16/share) vs $22.5M in 2024
R&D down 32% to $11.5M; G&A up 48% to $9.5M
Four foundry relationships incl. SilTerra and GlobalFoundries; 1.6T transceiver chip returns expected Q2 2026
2026 revenue mainly material supply and NRE; volume/licensing revenue not before 2027
January 2026 offering: $32.8M plus $4.9M over-allotment (per Quartr summary)
short_quotes: Yves LeMaitre (CEO) described 2025 as an "execution year".

earnings_calls.summary: There was no traditional Q3 2025 earnings call; the 10-Q was filed Nov 14, 2025 and CEO Yves LeMaitre hosted a separate business update call on Nov 25 covering strategic progress, technical milestones and the business-model repositioning. Earlier in the month (Nov 4) the company announced a Fortune Global 500 company had entered Stage 3 of its design-win cycle and that it was adding a second silicon photonics foundry alongside AMF.
key_points: Fortune Global 500 prospect moved into Stage 3 'Prototype to Final Product' (Nov 4, 2025 release)
2026 plan: build and test EO-polymer-augmented silicon photonics chips toward a data-center product
